examples.question_text:
A camping set costs $\$1\,080$ cash, or a $\$120$ deposit and $24$ monthly instalments of $\$50$.
(a) Calculate the total paid on terms.
(b) Find the interest charged and the saving made by paying cash.
examples.solution_text:
(a) Total paid:
$\begin{aligned}\text{Total paid}&=\text{Deposit}+\text{Number of instalments}\times\text{Instalment amount}\\&=120+24\times50\\&=\$1\,320\end{aligned}$
(b) Interest charged:
$\begin{aligned}\text{Interest}&=\text{Total paid}-\text{Cash price}\\&=1\,320-1\,080\\&=\$240\end{aligned}$
Paying cash saves $\$240$.

examples.question_text:
A sound system costs $\$1\,200$ cash, or a $15\%$ deposit and $26$ fortnightly instalments of $\$45$.
Calculate the deposit, the total paid on terms and the saving made by paying cash.

A furniture package costs a total of $\$2\,760$ on terms, including a $\$360$ deposit. The remainder, including interest, is paid in $24$ equal monthly repayments.
Calculate each monthly repayment.
examples.solution_text:
Amount to repay after the deposit:
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}2\,760-360\\&=\$2\,400\end{aligned}$
Monthly repayment:
$\begin{aligned}\text{Repayment}&=\text{Total owing}\div\text{Number of repayments}\\&=2\,400\div24\\&=\$100\end{aligned}$

examples.question_text:
A computer costs $\$1\,500$. It is bought on terms with a $20\%$ deposit and simple interest charged at $8\%$ p.a. on the remaining balance for $18$ months.
Calculate the total cost of buying the computer on terms.
examples.solution_text:
Deposit:
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}0.20\times1\,500\\&=\$300\end{aligned}$
Balance owing:
$\begin{aligned}P&=1\,500-300\\&=\$1\,200\end{aligned}$
Convert the term to years: $n=18\div12=1.5$.
Interest on the balance:
$\begin{aligned}I&=Prn\\&=1\,200\times0.08\times1.5\\&=\$144\end{aligned}$
Total cost, including the deposit:
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}300+1\,200+144\\&=\$1\,644\end{aligned}$

examples.question_text:
A second-hand car costs $\$10\,500$. A buyer pays a $\$2\,500$ deposit and repays the balance over $3$ years in equal monthly repayments. Simple interest is charged at $9\%$ p.a. on the balance after the deposit.
Calculate each monthly repayment, to the nearest cent.
examples.solution_text:
Balance owing:
$\begin{aligned}P&=10\,500-2\,500\\&=\$8\,000\end{aligned}$
Interest on the balance:
$\begin{aligned}I&=Prn\\&=8\,000\times0.09\times3\\&=\$2\,160\end{aligned}$
Total owing after the deposit:
$\begin{aligned}A&=P+I\\&=8\,000+2\,160\\&=\$10\,160\end{aligned}$
There are $3\times12=36$ monthly repayments.
Monthly repayment:
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}10\,160\div36\\&\approx\$282.22\end{aligned}$

examples.question_text:
Shoes costing $\$320$ are bought through an interest-free scheme with $4$ equal instalments and no other purchase fees. Maximum total late fees are the lower of $25\%$ of the order value or $\$68$.
(a) Calculate each instalment.
(b) Find the interest paid if all instalments are paid on time.
(c) Calculate the maximum total late fees.
examples.solution_text:
(a) Each instalment is $320\div4=\$80$.
(b) The total paid is $4\times80=\$320$, so the interest paid is $\$0$.
(c) $25\%\times320=\$80$.
The lower of $\$80$ and $\$68$ is $\$68$, so the maximum total late fees are $\$68$.

examples.question_text:
An order costing $\$56$ is bought through an interest-free instalment scheme. A missed payment incurs an initial late fee of $\$10$ and a further fee of up to $\$7$ if it remains unpaid $7$ days later. Total late fees are capped at the lower of $25\%$ of the order value or $\$68$.
The initial fee has already been charged. Calculate the further late fee after $7$ days.
examples.solution_text:
Maximum total late fees:
$25\%\times56=\$14$.
The lower of $\$14$ and $\$68$ is $\$14$.
Amount remaining under the cap:
$14-10=\$4$.
The further fee is reduced to $\$4$ to keep total late fees within the cap.

examples.derivation: Instalments total 24 × $50 = $1,200. Adding the $120 deposit gives $1,320. Interest charged and cash saving are $1,320 − $1,080 = $240.
Deposit = 0.15 × $1,200 = $180. Instalments total 26 × $45 = $1,170. Total paid = $1,350; cash saving = $150.
The included deposit is already paid: $2,760 − $360 = $2,400 remains. Each repayment is $2,400 ÷ 24 = $100.
Deposit = 0.20 × $1,500 = $300; principal = $1,200. Eighteen months is 1.5 years. Simple interest = $1,200 × 0.08 × 1.5 = $144. Total cost = $300 + $1,200 + $144 = $1,644.
Principal = $10,500 − $2,500 = $8,000. Interest = $8,000 × 0.09 × 3 = $2,160. The remaining $10,160 is divided across 36 repayments: $282.222… rounds to $282.22.
Each instalment is $320 ÷ 4 = $80. Four instalments total $320, giving $0 interest. Twenty-five percent of $320 is $80; the lower maximum fee is $68.
The total fee cap is min(0.25 × $56, $68) = $14. After the initial $10 fee, $4 remains under the cap. The further fee is min($7, $4) = $4.
